claims: He explores the balance between divine intervention and human initiative, contrasting the overt miracles in the southern campaign with the more natural, human-led conquests in the north.
The class also discusses the significance of these events in the context of the Jewish people's transition from a miraculous existence in the desert to a more natural life in the land of Israel.
summary: Rabbi Tawil examines the events of Yehoshua chapter 10, focusing on the miraculous battle where the sun and moon stood still to allow the Jewish people to defeat the Amorite kings. He explores the balance between divine intervention and human initiative, contrasting the overt miracles in the southern campaign with the more natural, human-led conquests in the north. The class also discusses the significance of these events in the context of the Jewish people's transition from a miraculous existence in the desert to a more natural life in the land of Israel.
questions: Why did the Giv'onim deceive the Jewish people into making a peace treaty?
What is the significance of the sun and moon standing still during the battle?
How do different commentators view the miracle of the sun standing still?
Why does the narrative shift from overt miracles to human-led battles in the second half of the chapter?
What is the relationship between divine intervention and human free will?
